transcript.text: Samsung WD90T534DBW washer dryer - clothes are still damp at the end of the wash and dry programme. It's not that old. Is the heater going?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. It is unlikely to be a heater fault at this stage. The most common reason clothes come out damp in a washer-dryer is simply that the load was too big for the drying cycle. A machine like yours can wash 9kg, but it can only dry about half of that (around 5kg). If you put a full wet wash straight onto the drying programme, there isn't enough air circulation to remove all the moisture. 1. Was the load within the dry capacity? If it was very full, try drying half of it next time.
2. Fluff buildup here stops air from flowing, which is essential for drying. If the load was small enough and those parts are clean, we can then check if the machine is actually heating up.
I put in a full 9kg drum and wash and dry in one go, using Wash+Dry with Cupboard Dry. The manual says 6kg for drying, so I guess that's over. Should I try a smaller load?

Yes, absolutely. You should try a smaller load. Your machine can wash 9kg but only dry about 6kg. Putting a full 9kg wet load straight onto the drying programme simply doesn't give the clothes enough room for hot air to circulate properly, so they come out damp regardless of how well the heater works. That said, it is still worth doing two quick checks before you run that smaller load next time:
1. Check the lint filter (usually at the bottom front) and clean it if there is any fluff.
2. If your model has a condenser unit (often behind a small panel near the filter or inside the door rim), remove it and rinse it under warm water to clear out any trapped lint. Restricted airflow makes drying much slower, so keeping these clear ensures your smaller load dries efficiently.
